items.label: f01-snapshot-not-ids
items.front: Why does a weekly risk Report store computed rows instead of the student ids to recompute from?
items.back: A snapshot must keep saying what it said. Recomputing next month against today's grades answers a different question and rewrites history. That is also why period dates are stored as ISO strings in the Json payload.

items.label: f02-disabled-agent-no-run
items.front: Why does a run of an agent with no active manifest throw before any AgentRun row exists?
items.back: A Failed run claims "it ran and broke", which is more alarming than "it is switched off". A disabled agent should leave no trace of having been attempted, so the gate throws CONFLICT first.

items.label: f04-known-partials
items.front: Name two acceptance criteria that shipped partial, per fabledocs/03-progress.md.
items.back: US-20: the postmortem is not enqueueable as an AgentRun job, and closed terms do not yet reject new assignments or attendance. US-17: every agent run resolves its own manifest (four queries per review), with no cache on purpose.

items.label: f03-red-test-wrong-test
items.front: What lesson did the team record about red tests across US-13 to US-20?
items.back: A red test was usually a wrong test: three times the code was right and the assertion wrong (CSV quoting, a note count, an absence-streak threshold). The streak case became a new fixture pinning where the boundary really is.

items.prompt: An agent has four manifests: 1.0.9 (active), 1.0.10-beta.1 (active), 1.0.10 (active) and 2.0.0 (inactive). Which one does selectActiveVersion return?
items.explanation: Inactive rows are filtered out first, so 2.0.0 is never considered. compareSemver compares numerically (10 > 9), and a version without a pre-release suffix outranks the same core with one, so 1.0.10 beats 1.0.10-beta.1.

items.prompt: A student success review computes a base confidence of 85. Its three sub-agents report 90, 60 and 80. What does confidenceFromSubagents return?

choices.text: 73, as half the 25-point gap to the weakest child is taken off
85, since two of the three children are at least fairly sure
60, because a parent is capped at its weakest child exactly
77, the mean of the three children, rounded to a whole number

choices: 73, as half the 25-point gap to the weakest child is taken off
85, since two of the three children are at least fairly sure
60, because a parent is capped at its weakest child exactly
77, the mean of the three children, rounded to a whole number

items.explanation: The weakest child (60) is below the base, so the penalty is (85 - 60) / 2 = 12.5, and Math.round(72.5) is 73. The mean is deliberately not used, and confidence never rises.

items.prompt: A section has two grading periods: P1 weight 0.4, where the student averages 80%, and P2 weight 0.6, where every assignment is still NotStarted. What weightedAverage does calculateWeightedGradeSummary report?

choices.text: 56, the 0.4 and 0.6 weights applied to 80 and 40 points
null until every weighted period has some scored work
32, since the empty P2 counts as zero at its 0.6 weight
80, because P2 is dropped and its weight redistributed

choices: 56, the 0.4 and 0.6 weights applied to 80 and 40 points
null until every weighted period has some scored work
32, since the empty P2 counts as zero at its 0.6 weight
80, because P2 is dropped and its weight redistributed

items.explanation: A period with no scored work has a null average and is filtered out of `scored`; the weighted mean divides by the remaining total weight (0.4), so it equals P1's 80. Treating the empty period as zero is the alarming result the comment rules out.

items.prompt: A teacher's /my-work queue holds four ungraded submissions: Critical-risk student waiting 2 days, High waiting 8, Medium waiting 12, Low waiting 9. Which submission does rankGradingQueue put second?

choices.text: The Low-risk one waiting 9 days
The Critical-risk one waiting 2 days
The High-risk one waiting 8 days
The Medium-risk one waiting 12 days

choices: The Low-risk one waiting 9 days
The Critical-risk one waiting 2 days
The High-risk one waiting 8 days
The Medium-risk one waiting 12 days

items.explanation: Urgency is days waiting plus a risk weight (Critical 14, High 7, Medium 3, Low 0): 16, 15, 15 and 9. Critical leads; High and Medium tie at 15, and the tie breaks on daysWaiting, so Medium (12 days) comes before High (8).

items.prompt: Someone presses Generate for the school-wide weekly risk report on Friday 1 January 2027 (UTC). Which idempotency key does weeklyReportKey(null, date) build?

choices.text: report:weekly-risk:null:2026-W53
report:weekly-risk:school:2026-W53
report:weekly-risk:school:2027-W00
report:weekly-risk:school:2027-W01

choices: report:weekly-risk:null:2026-W53
report:weekly-risk:school:2026-W53
report:weekly-risk:school:2027-W00
report:weekly-risk:school:2027-W01

items.explanation: A null scope becomes "school". ISO weeks belong to the year of their Thursday: the week of Friday 1 January 2027 has its Thursday on 31 December 2026, and 2026 has 53 ISO weeks, so the key ends 2026-W53.

items.prompt: A Teacher, who holds agent:run, starts a GuardianCommunicationDraft run. Its active manifest lists requiredPermissions ["agent:run", "notification:manage"]. What does resolveManifest do?

choices.text: Refuses it, since a Teacher lacks notification:manage
Allows it, but records the run as Failed for later review
Refuses it, since a Teacher can only target own students
Allows it, since holding agent:run is enough to run agents

choices: Refuses it, since a Teacher lacks notification:manage
Allows it, but records the run as Failed for later review
Refuses it, since a Teacher can only target own students
Allows it, since holding agent:run is enough to run agents

items.explanation: Manifest permissions are checked with assertCan in addition to agent:run. The Teacher branch of canPerform grants agent:run but not notification:manage, so the gate throws.

items.prompt: jobService.enqueue is called with idempotencyKey "digest:student_maya:week_2026_21", and a job with that key already exists in status Succeeded. What happens?

choices.text: A unique-constraint error surfaces, as the key is already taken
A new Queued job is created under that key plus a timestamp suffix
The Succeeded job is returned unchanged and nothing new is made
The Succeeded job is reset to Queued and its attempts set to 0

choices: A unique-constraint error surfaces, as the key is already taken
A new Queued job is created under that key plus a timestamp suffix
The Succeeded job is returned unchanged and nothing new is made
The Succeeded job is reset to Queued and its attempts set to 0

items.explanation: Only in-flight jobs (Queued, Running, Retrying) are deduplicated. A finished job with the key is history, so a new row is created, and its key gets ":" plus Date.now() so the unique constraint still holds.

items.prompt: A student has four records: 90 of 100 graded; a Late submission worth 100 with no score yet; a Submitted, ungraded one worth 100; and a Missing one worth 50. What average does calculateGradeSummary return?

choices.text: 36%, from 90 earned over 250 possible
About 25.7%, from 90 earned over 350 possible
90%, as only graded work counts toward the average
60%, from 90 earned over 150 possible

choices: 36%, from 90 earned over 250 possible
About 25.7%, from 90 earned over 350 possible
90%, as only graded work counts toward the average
60%, from 90 earned over 150 possible

items.explanation: Missing adds its points to the denominator. Since US-06 a Late submission with no score does too. Submitted-but-ungraded work is deliberately left out. So 90 / (100 + 100 + 50) = 36%.

items.prompt: A seat opens in section_algebra_a, and the office presses Promote on a waitlisted student who has since been marked Withdrawn from the school. What does decideWaitlistPromotion return?

choices.text: Refused: the section is still at capacity after the change
Refused: the student is no longer eligible for enrollment
Allowed, and the student is set back to an active status
Allowed, because a seat is open and the record is Waitlisted

choices: Refused: the section is still at capacity after the change
Refused: the student is no longer eligible for enrollment
Allowed, and the student is set back to an active status
Allowed, because a seat is open and the record is Waitlisted

items.explanation: Promotion re-checks eligibility as well as capacity. A Withdrawn or Graduated student is refused before capacity is looked at, so a closed record is not quietly re-activated.

items.prompt: Last week's risk snapshot did not include Priya. This week she appears at Critical. Where does diffReports put her?

choices.text: In biggestMovers, with a delta measured from zero
In newlyElevated, as a jump into the Critical band
In added only, not in newlyElevated
In both added and newlyElevated at the same time

choices: In biggestMovers, with a delta measured from zero
In newlyElevated, as a jump into the Critical band
In added only, not in newlyElevated
In both added and newlyElevated at the same time

items.explanation: A student absent from the previous snapshot goes to `added` and the loop moves on, so she is never compared for elevation or counted as a mover (her delta is null). Appearing at Critical is not the same as becoming critical.

items.prompt: A Mon/Wed/Fri class has sessions on Mon, Wed, Fri and the next Mon. The student has Absent records on Mon, Fri and the next Mon, and no record at all for Wed. What longest streak does findLongestAbsenceStreak return with and without those sessionDates?

choices.text: 3 with sessionDates, and 3 without them
2 with sessionDates; 3 without them
4 with sessionDates; 3 without them
2 with sessionDates, and 2 without them

choices: 3 with sessionDates, and 3 without them
2 with sessionDates; 3 without them
4 with sessionDates; 3 without them
2 with sessionDates, and 2 without them

items.explanation: Without sessions it walks the records only, and three Absent records in a row give 3. With sessions it walks the schedule, and a session with no record breaks the run ("we have no idea" is not evidence of absence), so the run is Fri plus Mon, 2.

items.prompt: An export cell holds the text =SUM(A1,B1), and another holds the number -5. What does escapeCsvValue write for each?

choices.text: =SUM(A1,B1) wrapped in quotes, and -5 left exactly as it is
"=SUM(A1,B1)" quoted, and "-5" quoted as a string too
"'=SUM(A1,B1)" quoted with a leading apostrophe, and '-5
'=SUM(A1,B1) with no quotes, and the bare number -5

choices: =SUM(A1,B1) wrapped in quotes, and -5 left exactly as it is
"=SUM(A1,B1)" quoted, and "-5" quoted as a string too
"'=SUM(A1,B1)" quoted with a leading apostrophe, and '-5
'=SUM(A1,B1) with no quotes, and the bare number -5

items.explanation: A value starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR gets an apostrophe prefix, applied to the rendered string, so negative numbers get it too. Then any value containing a comma, quote or newline is wrapped in quotes. The formula has a comma; -5 does not.

items.prompt: canRecordAttendance is asked about two records in an Active section, both inside the term: an Enrolled student dated 20 hours from now, and a Waitlisted student dated today. What does it decide?

choices.text: The Enrolled one is allowed; the Waitlisted one is refused
Both are allowed, as each student holds a seat or a place
The Waitlisted one is allowed; the future-dated one is refused
Both are refused: a future date is never accepted

choices: The Enrolled one is allowed; the Waitlisted one is refused
Both are allowed, as each student holds a seat or a place
The Waitlisted one is allowed; the future-dated one is refused
Both are refused: a future date is never accepted

items.explanation: Only Enrolled students may have attendance recorded. A date is refused only when it is more than 24 hours ahead, so 20 hours of slack is fine for a known trip.
